name: Question 11
problem:
The probability mass function of the independent random variables $X$ and $Y$ are given below.
$x$ $-1$ $0$ $1$
$f(x)$ $0.34$ $0.52$ $0.14$

$y$ $5$ $6$ $7$
$f(y)$ $0.15$ $0.6$ $0.25$

Find $\text{Var}[2X+7Y].$
worked_solution:
Recall that if $X$ and $Y$ are independent random variables and $a$ and $b$ are constants, then

$$
\text{Var}[aX+bY]={a}^{2}\text{Var}[X]+{b}^{2}\text{Var}[Y].
$$

Also, the variance of $X$ is determined by the formula 

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}.
$$

First, let's find $\text{Var}[X].$ If $X$ is defined on a sample space ${S}_{X}$, then

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\sum }_{x\in {S}_{X}}x\cdot f(x) \\  & =(-1)\cdot 0.34+0\cdot 0.52+1\cdot 0.14 \\  & =-0.2\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\sum }_{x\in {S}_{X}}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x) \\  & =1\cdot 0.34+0\cdot 0.52+1\cdot 0.14 \\  & =0.48.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =0.48-(-0.2)^{2} \\  & =0.44.\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, if $Y$ is defined on a sample space ${S}_{Y}$, then

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & ={\sum }_{y\in {S}_{Y}}y\cdot f(y) \\  & =5\cdot 0.15+6\cdot 0.6+7\cdot 0.25 \\  & =6.1\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{Y}^{2}] & ={\sum }_{y\in {S}_{Y}}{y}^{2}\cdot f(y) \\  & =25\cdot 0.15+36\cdot 0.6+49\cdot 0.25 \\  & =37.6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[Y] & =\text{E}[{Y}^{2}]-\text{E}[Y]^{2} \\  & =37.6-{6.1}^{2} \\  & =0.39.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[2X+7Y] & ={2}^{2}\text{Var}[X]+{7}^{2}\text{Var}[Y] \\  & =4(0.44)+49(0.39) \\  & =20.87.\end{aligned}
$$

Also, the variance of X is determined by the formula Var[X]=E[X2]−E[X]2.

E[X]=∑x∈SXx⋅f(x)=(−1)⋅0.34+0⋅0.52+1⋅0.14=−0.2

and

E[X2]=∑x∈SXx2⋅f(x)=1⋅0.34+0⋅0.52+1⋅0.14=0.48.

Therefore,

Var[X]=E[X2]−E[X]2=0.48−(−0.2)2=0.44.

Similarly, if Y is defined on a sample space SY, then

E[Y]=∑y∈SYy⋅f(y)=5⋅0.15+6⋅0.6+7⋅0.25=6.1

and

E[Y2]=∑y∈SYy2⋅f(y)=25⋅0.15+36⋅0.6+49⋅0.25=37.6.

Therefore,

Var[Y]=E[Y2]−E[Y]2=37.6−6.12=0.39.

Finally, we obtain

Var[2X+7Y]=22Var[X]+72Var[Y]=4(0.44)+49(0.39)=20.87.
